# Comprehension Report — DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md (Stage 6, Mode: REVIEW)

## What this proposes

The document proposes launching the app on the stores for the first time as **"Node"** — a multi-service platform (shops marketplace, P2P parcel, truck/fleet rental marketplace, ambulance) — while the original ride-hailing vertical stays fully built in the codebase but invisible to users. Four things change together: (1) ride is hidden behind a single runtime boolean on `platform_config` (`ride_vertical_enabled`), read by the client once per cold boot via a new public endpoint, failing closed to "hidden"; (2) the brand identity swaps to Node (name, bundle ID `com.node.bd`, deep-link scheme `node`, icons, splashes, palette, user-facing copy) in one atomic, irreversible commit before first store submission; (3) auth is re-organized user-first — user login is the first screen, an operator login/registration path sits at the bottom and routes into the three existing per-role wizards — while the one-phone-number/multi-role model is kept unchanged; (4) the services hub becomes the user home, and location permission + SOS move onto surviving surfaces so the launch product works end-to-end without any ride screen. Work is sequenced as six individually green stages (flag plumbing → identity rename → ride hide → auth re-organization → driver gating → flip the flag off), with re-enable proven by flipping the flag back on with no store update.

## How the existing system works, per this document

Today the app is a ride-hailing product: the customer landing is the ride-booking map, the splash shows a ride tagline, the first auth screen carries five role pills (rider, driver, shop owner, fleet owner, delivery man) that route through phone → OTP → per-role registration wizards, and after login a role-routing splash plus a "login-as" chooser (for multi-role accounts) sends each role to its home — rider/customer to the ride tabs, driver to the `(main)/(rider)` group, operators to their surfaces. Configuration lives in a `platform_config` DB table that is read fresh per request and written only by admins through `PATCH /api/admin/config`, which enforces an allowlist and owner-only keys. The repo is guarded by self-consistency gates (a testID map regenerated whenever `app/` changes, i18n braces/parity/orphan gates, Maestro flow checks, nav audits) that punish deletions — which is why the design hides ride instead of deleting it. The app has never been published, so the rename is a first-release identity decision, not a migration.

I verified the document's code citations before flagging anything: all spot-checked line references are exact (app/index.tsx:147 driver branch, :156 services-hub redirect, :200 "Your ride, your way"; app/_layout.tsx:172-173 driver gate; GlobalActionButtons.tsx:43-45 segment detection; phone-entry.tsx:157 "Ride" wordmark; welcome.tsx:45; login.tsx:77-84; login-as.tsx `ROLE_HOME`/`RESUBMIT_WIZARD`; common.json :3, :144-145, :183/:185, :1340, :1663), and every T2 asset referenced in `docs/Image/` exists, including the stray `android_adaptive_foreground_432 (1).png`. The document's "code facts verified" claim held everywhere I checked except Finding 2 below.

## Findings

**1. Severity: Major** — Affected Scope: Goals §G5 (line 47) vs Technical Plan §3 (line 180), §6 Rollout (line 243), Detailed Implementation Stage 2 heading (line 350).
The token **"G5" means two different things**. In Goals, G5 is "Services hub is the user home." But lines 180 ("device-verified before G5 (first store submission)"), 243 ("before G5"), and the Stage 2 heading ("irreversible after G5") use "G5" to mean a **first-store-submission gate** — a milestone this document never defines. Only line 180 carries the gloss; lines 243 and 350 don't. A fresh reader must either misread the sequencing constraint ("verified before the services hub is the home" — nonsense) or guess that G5 refers to gate vocabulary from outside this document. Rename the milestone (e.g., "before first store submission") or define the gate numbering.

**2. Severity: Major** — Affected Scope: Technical Plan §4 (line 219), Stage 4 table (lines 375-376).
The operator-login design hinges on a capability that doesn't exist and whose creation is never planned: "a **thin route wrapper** that renders the shared `phone-entry` flow with **`mode="operator"`** — no duplicated state machine." No section says `phone-entry` must gain an operator mode, and the Stage 4 row for `phone-entry.tsx` lists only the re-skin, flag-gated pills, and links. I verified the repo: `app/(auth)/phone-entry.tsx` has **no `mode` prop** (the only "mode" match is `resizeMode="contain"` at :151; role selection is internal `useState`, no route params are read). A naive reader cannot tell whether this mode is an existing feature or new work — and the "no duplicated state machine / no duplicated testIDs" claims rest on it. State explicitly that `phone-entry` gains the `mode` parameter in Stage 4.

**3. Severity: Major** — Affected Scope: Goals, Component C (lines 224-225), inventory rows 20-23 (lines 167-170), Stage 3 guard row (line 366), Stage 5.
The word "rider" carries **opposite meanings** and the mapping is never stated: the DB role `rider` is the *customer/User* role (line 225: "the chooser's 'Rider' row renders as" `User`), while the route group `(main)/(rider)` is the *driver* experience (it sits in the ride-route guard set next to "driver routing," and line 172 links it to "driver-framed hamburger items"). A fresh reader will most naturally read `(main)/(rider)` as customer screens — the exact inversion of reality. Line 172 conveys the linkage only implicitly. Add one sentence defining the legacy naming ("the `(rider)` route group is the driver experience; the `rider` DB role is the customer").

**4. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: inventory "Source ruling" column (lines 146-170), Stage 2 (line 354), Stage 4 (line 377).
Unresolvable provenance identifiers: "review Blocker 4" (rows 10, 11, 13-15), "review finding 6" (rows 20, 22-23), "review (codebase B-4)" (row 16), "(B-5)" (line 354), and "owner spec 3c" (line 377) cite numbered findings in review artifacts that the header (line 9) lists only as six unnamed-role report files — a reader can't tell which file holds which numbering, and "owner spec 3c" is linked nowhere. The inline dispositions make every build instruction complete, so these are provenance-only gaps, but they are weaker than the D-1…D-10 convention, which names its single authoritative file.

**5. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: inventory rows 12, 19, 20-21 vs Stage 3 (line 366).
The "Source ruling" column is semantically inconsistent: row 12's value is a phrase ("driver onboarding hidden"), not a ruling; row 19 cites "G6," which is a Goal (line 48), not a ruling. Also rows 20-21 say "gated by flag **AND** mount-guarded," but Stage 3 states "Zero edits inside ride screen files" — for these two screens the flag gating is realized *only* by the redirect guard, not in-file gating, which the row wording doesn't convey.

**6. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: Technical Plan §4 (line 221) vs Stage 4 (line 375).
The five role pills have a confusing dual home: Component C says they are "**relocated** into the operator dropdown's role list," while Stage 4 says they "render ONLY when the flag is on" on `phone-entry`. Both are true (the dropdown gets a new role list for the launch UX; the phone-entry pills survive behind the flag solely so driver Maestro flows stay valid, per D-6), but the reconciliation requires joining two sections. One clarifying clause would prevent a reader from "fixing" the apparent contradiction.

**7. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: Overview/G2 (lines 44, 241, 358) vs Component A (line 142).
"Dual defaults": G2 says the flag "defaults to **hidden** when the read fails (fail-closed)"; the rollout says Stage 1 "flag defaults **visible**." These describe different things (the client's fail-closed constant vs the seeded DB value), and Component A line 142 resolves it completely — but a hurried reader meets an apparent contradiction before reaching that paragraph.

**8. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: lines 32, 170, 236, 402.
Repo-gate jargon used by nickname: "testID map / i18n ratchet / Maestro flow checks" (line 32), "the LOCALE-ONLY ratchet" (line 236), "nav-integrity RESOLVED list" (line 170), "pre-commit harness replay," and "**execbro**" (line 402 — never defined; a naive reader can only infer it is a device-verification tool). Most gain inline elaboration on use (lines 303, 384), so this degrades rather than blocks comprehension.

**9. Severity: Nit** — Affected Scope: Technical Plan §3 (lines 182, 321), T2 palette (line 325), §6 rollout (lines 241-243).
Small underspecifications forcing invention: the replacement value for `expo-router.origin` is never given ("Node-branded origin" — the implementer must invent the URL); the palette entry "Green `#31B06A→#31B86A` family" is the only arrow notation in an otherwise plain value list (old→new is guessable but unstated); and the plan never motivates why the irreversible identity rename (stage 2) precedes the hide (stage 3) and auth re-organization (stage 4) — the sequence is clear, its rationale is not.

**No Blockers.** Every section connected: I could paraphrase the proposal, the current-state baseline, all six stages, and the decided-vs-open boundary (Open Questions: none; alternatives A–I rejected with reasons; D-1…D-10 rulings linked to their authoritative file). The findings above are precision repairs — the G5 collision, the unstated `mode="operator"` prerequisite, and the rider/(rider) terminology trap are the three a fresh reader would actually stumble on.
